title: Ambulance Operator Program
description:
The Santa Monica Fire Department launched its new in-house Ambulance Operator Program on Feb. 1, part of the city’s two-year Realignment Plan. The program establishes a dedicated team responsible for safely operating ambulances and supporting paramedic teams during emergency medical responses.

Previously, emergency medical transport was handled by a third-party provider. With this program, the Fire Department now provides these services using in-house personnel, vehicles and equipment, helping improve response efficiency across the community.

The program is projected to generate approximately $7 million in new revenue while strengthening emergency medical services for Santa Monica residents.
transcript_text: My name is Patrick Noli. I am the emergency medical services battalion chief for the Santa Monica Fire Department. The ambulance operator program is another exciting initiative that the fire department in the city have undergone. We started back in September as a pilot with just two units providing ambulance transportation along with our contracted provider. And as of February 1st, the city and the fire department have assumed full control, providing all of the ambulance transportation for all of our emergency medical patients on all 911 calls. The AO program does a number of things. One, it brings full control of our ambulance model under the umbrella of the fire department, which allows us to integrate it seamlessly with uh our dispatching, with our paramedics. Each fire station throughout the community has a dedicated ambulance assigned to it. So if emergency occurs in your neighborhood, you're not only getting the closest fire engine, you're also getting the closest ambulance as well. We implement all the training for our ambulance operators. All of the same procedures, protocols. It's really one cohesive response unit now, which is really good in regard to patient care and patient outcomes. Response times greatly improved. And the second thing is uh all of the reimbursement that comes with ambulance transportation is now able to be reinvested back into the program to further enhance training equipment and the hiring of additional personnel. Hi, I'm David McIll. I'm an ambulance operator for the city of Santa Monica. I'm a fifth generation city employee here in Santa Monica. My family's been serving the city for over 75 years throughout different departments in the city. So, it's been a passion of mine to be able to serve this community. I I grew up going to school here and my family's from this community and growing up I learned I wanted to become a firefighter. I'm just super proud to be able to be here and give back to a place that's given so much to me and to be able to grow in a place that I really feel is home. >> My name is Tommy Canrell. I'm an ambulance operator for the Santa Monica Fire Department. Being a part of the Santa Monica Fire Department AO program has been amazing. I'm a freshly new EMT. Everyone here has been very welcoming. Whether that be teaching me something I didn't know or just showing me around the city. It's been truly an honor to be an ambulance operator at Santa Monica Fire Department. Being an ambulance operator is great experience if you want to get into EMS or being a firefighter. Santa Monica has taught me so much and I'm only going to grow from here.
